statBlock.name: Bodak
statBlock.description: An undead devotee of Orcus. Orcus can recall anything the bodak witnesses and speak through it.

sections.Languages: Abyssal and the languages it spoke in life.
sections.Damage resistances: Cold, fire, and necrotic damage. It also resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
sections.Traits:
Aura of Annihilation. The bodak can turn the aura on or off as a bonus action. While it is on, creatures within 30 ft. of the bodak take 5 necrotic damage when they end their turns there. Fiends and undead are immune to the aura.
Death Gaze. When a creature that can see the bodak’s eyes starts its turn within 30 ft. of the bodak, the bodak can force a DC 13 Constitution save. It must be able to see the creature and must not be incapacitated. A failure by 5 or more drops the target to 0 HP unless it is immune to frightened. A target that fails without dropping to 0 HP takes 16 (3d10) psychic damage. A creature that isn’t surprised can avert its eyes at the start of its turn and skip this save. It then attacks the bodak with disadvantage until its next turn starts. If it looks at the bodak before then, it makes the save immediately.
Sunlight Hypersensitivity. The bodak takes 5 radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. It has disadvantage on attacks and ability checks while in sunlight.
Undead Nature. The bodak needs no air, food, drink, or sleep.
Ravaged Soul. Restoring a bodak to its former life requires Wish or comparable magic.
sections.Actions:
Fist. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d4 + 2) bludgeoning plus 9 (2d8) necrotic damage.
Withering Gaze. One visible creature within 60 ft. makes a DC 13 Constitution save. It takes 22 (4d10) necrotic damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Encounter context: Maze of Death, p. 162. Two bodaks emerge unharmed from the Sphere of Annihilation in area 49B and hunt in the maze. They drag anyone they kill back into the sphere. They return to the sphere when they think the maze is empty.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 215.

statBlock.name: Firenewt Warlock of Imix
statBlock.description: A priest of Imix who commands firenewt raids and claims the best spoils for the cult.

sections.Armor: AC 13 while it has Mage Armor.
sections.Senses: Darkvision 120 ft., including in magical darkness.
sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The warlock breathes both air and water.
Imix’s Blessing. The warlock gains 5 temporary HP when it reduces an enemy to 0 HP.
sections.Innate spellcasting: The warlock uses Charisma to cast Mage Armor on itself at will, without material components.
sections.Spellcasting:
Third-level warlock. Charisma is its spellcasting ability (save DC 12, +4 for spell attacks). Both spell slots cast at 2nd level and recharge on a short or long rest.
At-will cantrips. Fire Bolt, Guidance, Light, Mage Hand, and Prestidigitation.
1st- and 2nd-level spells known (two 2nd-level slots). Burning Hands, Flaming Sphere, Hellish Rebuke, and Scorching Ray.
sections.Actions: Morningstar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 5 (1d8 + 1) piercing damage.
sections.Encounter context: Hrakhamar, pp. 62–63. A warlock supervises the forge, two in the stores debate whether to accuse that warlock of heresy, and two fight to the death with Firenewt Warriors at the shrine. A heavy patrol can include a warlock riding a Giant Strider (p. 199).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 219.

statBlock.name: Firenewt Warrior
statBlock.description: An amphibious soldier of Imix trained to raid and patrol volcanic Chult.

sections.Traits: Amphibious. The warrior breathes both air and water.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Scimitar attacks.
Scimitar. Melee weapon attack, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 4 (1d6 + 1) slashing damage.
Spit Fire (recharges after a short or long rest). One creature within 10 ft. makes a DC 11 Dexterity save. It takes 9 (2d8) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
sections.Encounter context: Valley of Lost Honor and Hrakhamar, pp. 42, 61–63. Four mounted warriors typically patrol Ataaz Yklwazi. The eight warriors at the smelter are surprised unless the party draws attention. Two warriors and two Firenewt Warlocks of Imix defend the shrine to the death. For the wilderness patrol on p. 199, roll 1d4 warriors for a light patrol or 2d4 warriors and one warlock for a heavy patrol, with one Giant Strider per rider. These patrols aim to knock opponents unconscious and take them captive.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 219.

statBlock.name: Flail Snail
statBlock.description: A slow earth elemental with a brightly colored shell and five mace-tipped tentacles.

sections.Traits:
Antimagic Shell. The snail saves against spells with advantage. Spell attacks against it have disadvantage. Roll a d6 when the snail succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or a spell attack misses it.
1–2. An area or multitarget spell fails entirely. A spell aimed solely at the snail leaves it unharmed and rebounds at the caster with the original slot level, save DC, spell attack bonus, and spellcasting ability.
3–4. Nothing else happens.
5–6. Each creature within 30 ft. of the snail makes a DC 15 Constitution save. It takes 1d6 force damage per level of the spell on a failure or half as much on a success.
Flail Tentacles. The snail starts with five. Every turn on which it takes at least 10 damage costs it one tentacle. As long as one remains, all dead tentacles grow back in 1d4 days. Losing the last tentacle sends the snail into its shell with total cover. It wails audibly out to 600 ft. until it dies 5d6 minutes later. Regenerate or other limb-restoring magic can stop it from dying.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make one Flail Tentacle attack per surviving tentacle, all against the same target.
Flail Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. A hit deals 6 (1d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage.
Scintillating Shell (recharges after a short or long rest). Until the end of the snail’s next turn its shell casts bright light for 30 ft. and dim light for another 30 ft. Creatures that can see the snail attack it with disadvantage during that time. Any creature in the bright light that can see the snail when it activates this effect must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or become stunned until the light goes out.
Shell Defense. The snail retracts into its shell, raising AC by 4 until it comes out. Emerging takes a bonus action on its turn.
sections.Encounter context: Unkh takes the form of a flail snail in Omuan stories (pp. 92, 102–103). A DC 10 Wisdom (Survival) check determines which way a snail was traveling from its slime trail (p. 199). An intact shell weighs about 250 lb. and is worth 2,500 gp.
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 220.

statBlock.name: Froghemoth
statBlock.description: An amphibious swamp predator with four long tentacles. It leaves only its three-eyed stalk above water while waiting for prey.

sections.Traits:
Amphibious. The froghemoth breathes both air and water.
Shock Susceptibility. After taking lightning damage, it suffers these effects until the end of its next turn. Its speed is halved, its AC and Dexterity saves take a −2 penalty, and it loses reactions and Multiattack. On its turn it must choose between an action and a bonus action.
sections.Actions:
Multiattack. Make two Tentacle attacks. The froghemoth may also use either Tongue or Bite.
Tentacle. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. A hit deals 19 (3d8 + 6) bludgeoning damage. It also grapples a Huge or smaller creature (escape DC 16). Each of the four tentacles can hold one creature and can’t be used on another target while holding it.
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +10 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 22 (3d10 + 6) piercing damage and swallows a Medium or smaller creature. The gullet holds up to two creatures. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover against attacks and effects originating outside the froghemoth, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of the froghemoth’s turns. If a creature inside deals at least 20 damage in one turn, the froghemoth must pass a DC 20 Constitution save at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land prone within 10 ft. If the froghemoth dies, the restraint ends and a swallowed creature can spend 10 ft. of movement to leave the corpse, exiting prone.
Tongue. One visible Medium or smaller creature within 20 ft. makes a DC 18 Strength save. On a failure, pull it to an empty space within 5 ft. of the froghemoth, which can then use Bite against that creature as a bonus action.
sections.Encounter context: Kubazan, the trickster god, takes the form of a froghemoth. At his shrine in Omu, a DC 14 Wisdom (Perception) check spots a froghemoth’s eyestalk in the murky, 6-ft.-deep pool. It attacks if someone disturbs the water or approaches the shrine, leaving the pool to pursue them (p. 97).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 221.

statBlock.name: Giant Strider
statBlock.description: A fast, birdlike reptilian monstrosity that willingly carries elite firenewt riders.

sections.Traits: Fire Absorption. When fire would damage the giant strider, it takes none and instead heals half the amount it would have taken.
sections.Actions:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 8 (1d8 + 4) piercing damage.
Fire Burst (recharge 5–6). Choose a visible point within 60 ft. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere centered there makes a DC 12 Dexterity save. It takes 14 (4d6) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success. The fire goes around corners and ignites flammable objects in the area that nobody wears or carries.
sections.Encounter context: Hrakhamar, p. 64. The firenewts keep twelve striders tethered in the mine cart bay. When a non-firenewt enters, the mounts become restless. Starting the following round, 1d3 break loose each round and attack. The striders spare firenewts, who can ride them with the standard Mounted Combat rules. A Firenewt Warrior patrol in the Valley of Lost Honor travels on these mounts (pp. 42, 83, 199).
sections.Printed source: Tomb of Annihilation, Appendix D, p. 222.
